name: Tata Consumer Products Ltd.
business_summary: Tata group's FMCG company: India tea (Tata Tea, Tetley), coffee (Tata Coffee, Eight O'Clock), salt (Tata Salt), Tata Sampann pulses/spices, Soulfull, ready-to-drink (Tata Gluco Plus, Himalayan, NourishCo), Capital Foods (Ching's, Smith & Jones) and Organic India, an International business (UK, US, Canada, Australia) and a stake in the Tata Starbucks JV (model knowledge on portfolio). Q2 FY27: revenue Rs5,661cr (+14%), EBITDA +18% to Rs794cr (margin 14.0%), PAT ~Rs470cr (+16%). India tea/coffee revenue fell 1% on flat volume while growth businesses grew 40% (Sampann +57%, RTD +47%). Stock Rs1,077; P/E 62, P/B 4.8, ROE 7.4%; mcap Rs1.07 lakh cr.

revenue_mix.segment: India foods (salt, Sampann, Soulfull, Capital Foods, Organic India)
Non-branded and other (plantations, Tata Coffee exports, NourishCo)

exposures.mechanism: Tea and coffee raw material ~20% of revenue (tea/coffee ~40% of COGS, COGS ~50% of sales; model estimate). +15% cost => +3% of revenue; ~50% recovered through price hikes in 6 months => net 1.5% of revenue => EBITDA -10.7% at 14% margin; x EV/MCap 1.05 x persistence 0.3 => -3.4. Q2: higher tea and salt costs cut India tea/coffee profit share (Investywise); company has raised prices (Rediff 2026-11-04).

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs5,661cr +14%, EBITDA +18%, margin 14.0%; India tea/coffee -1%; growth businesses +40%

exposures.mechanism: Packaging ~6% of revenue; +10% => 0.6% of revenue; 40% passed through => 0.36% => EBITDA -2.6% x 1.05 x 0.3 => -0.8.

Freight, fuel and polymer packaging ~4% of revenue linked to oil; +10% Brent => +0.2% of revenue after pass-through => EBITDA -1.4% x 1.05 x 0.3 + indirect => -0.5. Agrees with pack (-0.27, t -0.7, not significant).

Tea, salt and staples are ~35% rural. +5pp rural growth => volumes +1.5% => revenue +1.5% x incremental margin 30% / base 14% => EBITDA +3.2% x 1.05 x persistence 0.5 => +1.7. India tea/coffee volume flat in Q2 (subdued demand).

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs5,661cr +14%, EBITDA +18%, margin 14.0%; India tea/coffee -1%; growth businesses +40%

exposures.mechanism: Premium/growth portfolio (Sampann, RTD, Capital Foods, Organic India, Starbucks JV) is urban-skewed; growth businesses +40% in Q2, Sampann +57%, RTD +47%. +5pp urban demand => revenue +2% x 30%/14% => EBITDA +4.3% x 1.05 x 0.5 => +2.3.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs5,661cr +14%, EBITDA +18%, margin 14.0%; India tea/coffee -1%; growth businesses +40%

exposures.mechanism: Food CPI 7.74% (Sep). +2pp squeezes household budgets and trade-down: volumes -0.5% => EBITDA -1% x 1.05 x 0.5 => -0.5; plus input inflation that exceeds price hikes => -0.8. Offsetting: pricing power on branded tea/salt.

evidence.note: CPI 5.54% in Sep 2026, food inflation 7.74% (CNBC/ET headlines)

exposures.mechanism: 62x P/E, 4.8x book, ROE 7.4% (screener): long-duration; net cash-light balance sheet. +25bp G-sec => ~-2% on multiple at 50% CoE pass-through => -1.0.

evidence.note: P/E 62, BV Rs223, ROE 7.4%, mcap Rs1.07 lakh cr; Q2 OPM 14%
India 10y G-sec ~7.4-7.5% in Oct 2026, multi-year high (Reuters/ET headlines); Nov outlook 7.25-7.35%

exposures.mechanism: International ~30% of revenue (UK, US, Canada, Australia; EBITDA share ~20%) gains from rupee weakness; imported coffee, tea blends, nuts/pulses ~8% of revenue lose. +3%: +0.6% EBITDA translation vs -1.7% import cost => ~-1% x 1.05 x 0.5 => -0.5. Pack: -0.58 (t -0.5), agrees in sign.
Pack: +0.88 per +5 VIX points, t +2.8 (market beta 0.90): defensive FMCG attracts rotation when risk-off. Kept at +0.8 (shrunk slightly toward fundamentals; mostly removed by market demeaning).

Value-added/branded mix (Sampann, Capital Foods, RTD) gains from premiumisation: +1 => growth businesses +2pp growth (15% of revenue) => revenue +0.3% at higher margin => EBITDA +0.8% persistent => +1.0.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs5,661cr +14%, EBITDA +18%, margin 14.0%; India tea/coffee -1%; growth businesses +40%

exposures.mechanism: Quick commerce channels are over-indexed for Capital Foods, Sampann and RTD; +1 => channel growth adds ~0.5% to revenue at accretive margin => +0.8.
Packaged food/beverage GST cuts lower shelf prices; +1 (~2-5pp) => volumes +1.5-2% => EBITDA +3.5% x 1.05 x 0.3 => +1.0. Tea/salt already low-rate, so effect smaller than for other FMCG.
